subject: Planned eastus3 service refresh — staged node restarts & driver update
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: acme-product@example.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned eastus3 service refresh — staged node restarts & driver update

Hi Team —

We’re scheduling a planned, staggered service refresh in the eastus3 region the week of July 5 to apply a vetted kernel/driver update to a subset of inference hosts. This is a targeted maintenance to address a storage driver regression we observed under specific IO patterns; it improves KV cache resilience for long-running sessions.

High-level details:
- Maintenance window: July 6–8, 2027 (UTC windows below).
- Expected per-node disruption: 2–5 minutes while the host drains and restarts. We will sequence restarts to avoid cluster-wide impacts.
- Impact to customers: transient 503s on affected shards for a few minutes in a rolling pattern; overall cluster throughput should remain within normal variance.
- Canaries first: 10% of host pool will run the update and validate traffic for 2 hours before broader rollout.

Schedule (local UTC windows):
- 2027-07-06 02:00–06:00 UTC — canary hosts (10%)
- 2027-07-06 08:00–20:00 UTC — staged group A
- 2027-07-07 00:00–20:00 UTC — staged group B
- 2027-07-08 00:00–20:00 UTC — fallback / catch-up window

What we’ve done so far:
- Engineering (Markus) validated the driver build on identical hardware and ran 48h perf regressions.
- Ops (Neha) prepared automated drain/playback steps and rollback images.
- CS (Marissa) asked me to surface any customer-impacting timing so you can schedule internal QA.

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook + rollback instructions), canary-validation-checklist.csv (what we will verify during canary).

Action items for you:
- Please confirm if the July 6–8 window conflicts with any planned customer events you know of.
- If you’d like a dedicated pre-rollout call for your SREs, propose a time (we can do 2027-07-05 15:00–16:00 UTC).

If you have strict region blackout requirements, reply and we’ll apply an opt-out for your account for this cycle (we’ll reschedule with a separate migration path).

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

2) Do you have an estimated number of active sessions we should expect to see dropped during the 2–5 minute restarts (ballpark)?

Subject: Re: Planned eastus3 service refresh — staged node restarts & driver update

Hi Kenta —

Great questions. Quick answers below and I’ve pulled Neha/Markus into thread for any further tech details.

1) Canary endpoints: we’ll provide exact host ids and ephemeral IP ranges 24 hours before the canary run. They are not fixed for every maintenance cycle to sandbox blast radius. If you need CIDR blocks to pre-whitelist now, we can share the ephemeral pool we’ll use for July 6 canary: 10.240.32.0/22 and 198.51.100.0/25 (will confirm 24h prior).

2) Session drop estimate: for your workload profile we expect ~0.2–0.6% active session interruption during active canary restarts (absolute numbers depend on current traffic). We’ll track and share canary metrics live.

Pre-rollout call: 2027-07-05 15:00 UTC works for our team. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Neha/Markus: can you confirm the rollback window if the canary shows an unexplained regression?

Thanks,
Karthik

----- Message 4 (post-maintenance recap) -----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: acme-product@example.com, ops@bluecloud.io
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Eastus3 refresh complete — brief recap & follow-ups

Hi all —

We completed the staged refresh in eastus3 across July 6–8 (canary + two staged waves). Summary below:

What happened
- Canary (10%): Passed validation after 90 minutes of production traffic. No regressions observed for KV cache persistence or request latency.
- Staged waves: Hosts were drained and restarted per playbook; median host restart time 3.2 minutes.
- Observed impact: brief (<=5 min) increase in 503s localized to restarted shards during each host cycle. End-user request latencies outside of those windows were unchanged.

Root cause & fix
- Root cause: a storage driver regression under specific aggregated IO patterns; the new driver includes a stability patch validated by engineering.
- Fix: driver update + small kernel tuning parameter (applied during restart).

Did anything go wrong
- No customer-facing incidents escalated. One canary host showed elevated write stalls at T+24m; we rolled that host back, investigated, and re-included it after a secondary verification cycle. The rollback path worked as designed.

Metrics & artifacts
- Median host restart: 3.2 minutes
- Canary validation dashboard: https://redwood.app/incident/INC-20270628
- Post-run runbook and logs: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf (attached)

Follow-ups & mitigations
- Engineering: add a short synthetic workload test to the validation suite to catch this IO pattern (owner: markus_klein).
- Ops: update runbook with clearer rollback signal thresholds (owner: neha_kapoor).
- CS: Marissa will reach out to affected customers with a short note (owner: marissa_cole).

If you’d like additional telemetry from your org’s slice during the window, reply to this thread and we’ll extract hourly canary snapshots.

Thanks for your coordination and patience — please reach out if you want a deeper postmortem call.

Best,
Karthik

Attachments referenced: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf, canary-validation-checklist.csv
